fields.meta_title: Free Client Onboarding Questionnaire Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a client onboarding questionnaire that tracks account access, chases missing answers and routes each client to the right lead. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Client Onboarding Questionnaire That Starts the Work
fields.hero_description: Create a client onboarding questionnaire that shows each client only their sections and reminds them about anything still open.
fields.features_heading: What Happens After the Client Hits Submit
fields.features_subheading: A client onboarding questionnaire earns its place once the answers turn into work. These six pieces handle that part.
fields.feature_1:
Sections that follow the service bought

Show each client only the sections for the services on their contract. A retainer client answers brand voice questions, while a one-off project skips ahead to scope and deadlines.
fields.feature_2:
Account access tracked row by row

List every account the work depends on and let the client tick each one once access is shared. You see what is still missing at a glance, without a single password changing hands.
fields.feature_3:
Reminders for whatever is still open

Email the client contact when an answer or file is still outstanding after the delay you set. Each reminder names the items left, and reminders stop once the last one arrives.
fields.feature_4:
Answers that become the first tasks

Turn specific answers into work that can start on day one: a shot list, a hardware audit, a first content calendar. Each task links back to the client response that created it.
fields.feature_5:
Routing by account size or service

Send each finished questionnaire to the teammate who owns that kind of client. Large accounts can reach a senior lead by Slack message, and the rest join the standard queue.
fields.feature_6:
Your onboarding app, as code you keep

On paid plans, export the codebase to your GitHub repo when the questionnaire grows into a client portal. A developer can extend it later, and every client record stays where it is.
fields.why_title: Why Use Emergent for Client Onboarding?
fields.why_description: A template collects answers and leaves the follow-up to you. Emergent builds the reminders, routing and records around them.

fields.tab_content_1:
No kickoff call until all four accounts are shared

Fernbrook Social asks each new client to share access on all four social accounts, never a password. Harbor Coffee Roasters has shared three. With TikTok missing, the kickoff call stays unbooked, and Dana Whitlock, Harbor's marketing manager, gets a reminder after two days.
fields.tab_content_2:
A 24-shot list built from one questionnaire

Ollie Park shoots half-day brand sessions. For Larkspur Ceramics, the questionnaire asked which shots the owner wanted in each spot: 10 in the studio, eight on the shop floor and six on the street outside. The answers became a 24-shot list grouped by location, with the client's notes beside each shot.
fields.tab_content_3:
Laptops over five years old flagged before day one

Cobalt IT took on Marsh Dental, a practice with 42 staff across two offices. Its questionnaire asks the office manager to list every laptop with its user and age. Cobalt marks any laptop over five years old for replacement. Of 38 laptops, five land on the replacement list in the kickoff report before the technician's first visit.
fields.tab_content_4:
Who leads onboarding depends on seat count

Tallyhub sells scheduling software to clinics and salons. Its questionnaire asks each new customer how many seats it bought. Accounts with 200 seats or more go to Nadia Rahman, the implementation lead, as a Slack message. Smaller accounts start a three-week self-serve plan, with a welcome email on day one.

fields.howto_title: How to Write an Onboarding Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a client onboarding questionnaire that clients finish before the kickoff call.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what the first week depends on
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give account access its own page
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Require only what blocks the work
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the first week of work needs from the client: approvals, files, account access, a budget. Anything outside that list belongs in a later check-in. A questionnaire that asks only what the team will use gets finished, and finished answers are what you need.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Group questions under the service the client is paying for. A monthly retainer needs brand and audience sections, while a one-time project needs scope, a deadline and the person who signs off. Each client sees only their own sections, which keeps the form short.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the account access requests on their own page, one row per account, with a two-line how-to for each. Ask the client to give you a role on the account instead of sending a password. A checkbox per row shows what is still missing.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Mark a question required only when the team cannot start without the answer, and leave the rest optional. Required answers and pending access decide when the kickoff call can be booked. The client sees a short list of what is left, not the whole form again.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set a due date and the reminders
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick a due date that leaves time to read the answers before kickoff. When an item is still open after two days, email the client contact the exact items left. A second reminder can go to the account owner on your side.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Every answer is stored against the client, in a searchable table. Then pick the answers that start work: a seat count that picks the onboarding track, shot choices for the photographer, a hardware list for the technician who visits first.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Fill it in as your newest client
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the link on a phone, answer as a new client would and skip one access row on purpose. Check that the reminder arrives and the kickoff stays unbooked. Then finish the row and confirm the completed answers reach the right person.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is question lists (Content Snare, HubSpot, OnRamp, Financial Cents, two social media agency guides) and two template galleries (Jotform, Fillout). Each one hands over 20 questions and stops at the submit button. This page treats the questionnaire as the start of the engagement: answers that hold a kickoff until the last account login arrives, become a photographer's shot list, flag old hardware before an IT firm's first site visit, and decide which onboarding track a software customer gets. The FAQ covers the related searches on templates, Word and PDF versions, questions to ask and niche versions for photographers and social media work.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Client Onboarding Questionnaire That Starts the Work' and title 'Free Client Onboarding Questionnaire Builder' state the whole job.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is question lists and template galleries; FAQ gives questions to ask, free, Word, PDF, timing, form vs questionnaire, photography and social media versions; how-to is specific.

specificity.evidence: Agency vocabulary: 'share access on all four social accounts, never a password', 'kickoff call stays unbooked', '200 seats or more go to Nadia Rahman'.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on verbs ('Show each client', 'List every account', 'Email the client contact', 'Turn specific answers').

craft.evidence: QC Q-checks clean; reviewer added the missing full stop to hero_prompt (QC re-run TOTAL 0).

voice.evidence: Concrete businesses and numbers ('10 in the studio, eight on the shop floor and six on the street outside').

truth.evidence: Definition matches Content Snare; social access matches Sked Social; bookkeeping questions match Financial Cents; numbers agree (10+8+6=24, 5 of 38, 240 seats in tab and cover).

distinct.evidence: Agency, photography, IT and software stories; wedding photography, website design questionnaire and intake form linked, not headlined.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, hub link in item 2, sibling links 'intake form', 'wedding photography questionnaire', 'website design questionnaire'.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy: '3 shared', 'TikTok access still missing', 'Sent after two days', '24 shots for Larkspur Ceramics', '5 of 38 to replace', 'Sent to Nadia Rahman' 'By Slack message'.
